newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-EX-CY YOUNG AWARD WINNER MARK DAVIS SIGNS WITH ARIZONA.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-EX-CY YOUNG AWARD WINNER MARK DAVIS SIGNS WITH ARIZONA.

text.p: Left-hander Mark Davis, the 1989 Cy Young Award winner, became the first player with major-league experience to sign with the expansion Arizona Diamondbacks when he agreed to a minor-league contract Friday.
The 36-year-old Davis needs to hang on in the minors for the 1997 season if he wants to play for Diamondbacks when they start play in the National League in 1998.
Davis used a blazing fastball and one of the league's best curves to dominate out of the San Diego Padres' bullpen in the late 1980s. But arm problems derailed his career.

"Mark strongly believes that his physical problems are behind him and that he can be an effective major-league pitcher in certain situations," said Diamondsbacks vice president and general manager Joe Garagiola Jr. "We will give him the opportunity to prove it."
When Davis won the Cy Young, he recorded 44 saves in 48 chances and went 4-3 record with a 1.85 ERA in 92 2/3 innings over 70 appearances. He allowed just 66 hits and walked 31 with 92 strikeouts.

The following season, Davis signed a lucrative free-agent contract with the Kansas City Royals and failed miserably, ending up 2-7 with a 5.11 ERA in stints between the bullpen and the starting rotation.

He has the distinction of being traded for two different National League Most Valauble Players. In 1982, he was sent from the Philadelphia Phillies to the San Francisco Giants in the Joe Morgan deal. In 1987, he went from the Giants to the Padres in the Kevin Mitchell trade.
For his career, which has spanned parts of 14 major-league seasons, Davis is 51-84 with a 4.15 ERA and 96 saves. He has not pitched in the majors since appearing in 20 games for San Diego in 1994.
